seo.title: Metformin: Uses, Dosage, Side Effects | Doctors Hub
seo.description: Complete guide to Metformin (Metformin HCl). Learn uses, dosage, side effects, warnings, and drug interactions.

composition: Metformin HCl — consult product label for exact strength and excipients.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (first-line therapy in many patients)
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) — off-label use under specialist care
Prediabetes in selected patients per clinician guidance
howItWorks: Metformin reduces glucose production in the liver, improves insulin sensitivity in muscle tissue, and may reduce intestinal glucose absorption. It does not cause hypoglycaemia when used alone.

dosage.adults: As directed by physician. Typical adult dose varies by condition and formulation.
dosage.children: Pediatric dosing must be weight-based. Consult pediatrician.
dosage.elderly: May require dose adjustment in elderly patients.
dosage.notes: Take with food if stomach upset occurs unless otherwise directed.

missedDose: Take as soon as remembered unless near next dose. Do not double dose.
overdose: Seek immediate medical attention. Contact nearest hospital or poison control.
warnings: Common brands in India include Glycomet and Obimet.
pregnancy: Consult doctor before use during pregnancy. Risk-benefit assessment required.
breastfeeding: Consult doctor. Some medicines pass into breast milk.
kidneyDisease: Dose adjustment may be needed. Inform your nephrologist.
liverDisease: Use with caution. Liver function monitoring may be required.
driving: Avoid driving if dizziness or drowsiness occurs.
alcohol: Avoid alcohol unless approved by doctor. May increase side effects.
foodInteraction: Take as directed with or without food per physician advice.
drugInteractions: Certain antibiotics — inform your doctor of all medicines
storage: Store in cool, dry place below 25°C. Keep away from children.

faqs.question: Should metformin be taken with food?
faqs.answer: Yes. Taking it with meals reduces stomach upset. Extended-release forms may have different timing — follow your prescription.
